title: The x86-64 ABI
description: Place arguments, results and callee-saved registers the way x86-64 code requires, including why a system call moves the return address into r10 instead of rcx.
author: Underlayer
completion_criteria: Read all 6 concepts, reproduce the 126 checks in courses/x86abi/assets/samples/crosscheck.py, then break the positive control on purpose -- delete the `pushq %rbx` from control.s -- and make group H2 fail by name

modules.title: The Frame: What a Call Owes Whom
The Second Description: Unwinding and the Audit

concepts.title: The Calling Convention, and the Register That Wasn't
concepts.description: Six argument registers and their NUMBERS, audited by name against a written specification at four optimisation levels -- and the fourth argument is rcx, not r10, because a bare syscall instruction writes the return RIP into rcx and a call pushes it onto the stack instead. Both halves measured, in one section.

concepts.title: The Stack Frame, the Red Zone, and Two Rules
concepts.description: The 128-byte red zone, and the measurement that shows why it is for LEAF functions only: the first eight bytes of it are the return-address slot and `call` writes them. And the alignment rule is TWO rules, because a call and a tail jmp want opposite adjustments.

concepts.title: Callee-Saved and Caller-Saved, by Experiment
concepts.description: Not a table: a callee that tramples r12 and a conforming one, and which of the caller's values survive. Then the two floating-point control registers, which point in OPPOSITE directions, and a linter that read 4,561 glibc functions and needed a positive control to prove it was looking at anything.

concepts.title: The One Place the ABI Describes Itself
concepts.description: A 176-byte register save area, and a caller that lies about %al: the arguments are not corrupted in transit, they are never looked at, and the consumer gets the PREVIOUS call's floating-point numbers back -- bit for bit, and through glibc's printf as well as through its own.

concepts.title: Unwinding, and the Second Language
concepts.description: The .cfi_* directives are a second, independent description of the same frame, and a program compiled with -fno-asynchronous-unwind-tables returns ONE frame from backtrace() where it returns seven without it: not a wrong answer, no answer.

concepts.title: Read the ABI Out of the Disassembly
concepts.description: The artifact, and the audit: 64 of 64 callers match a written specification at four optimisation levels, 4,561 functions of glibc are read for callee-saved violations, and the checker that found nothing in 9,255 functions had a ternary the wrong way round and had never once recognised a callee-saved register.
